provenance: Bodl. MS Arab. c 56 was recognized as probably coming from the Cairo Geniza only in July 2025. Athina Pfeiffer found photos online and brought them to the attention of Marina Rustow, who made the connection to the Geniza. Pfeiffer has written up her findings and will publish them. Fol. 1v has a pencilled note in the margin saying "Bought from Egypt through Prof. Sayce 1899" (? last digit effaced). Archibald Sayce was another known dealer of geniza material to the Bodleian. There is also a pencilled note on frontispiece of volume that says "Mostly from Werthheimer Jerusalem." Solomon Aaron Werthheimer was known to have sold geniza fragments to Schechter in Cambridge, Neubauer in Oxford, and Yellin in Jerusalem (for the JNUL) in the 1890s (see Jefferson 2022 p. 107). But some of Wertheimer's manuscripts may have come from Yemen, so a Cairo provenance isn't certain for every item in this volume.

Reinach III
provenance:
The Reinach manuscript is one sheet of paper held in the past by Theodore Reinach in Paris. 
On its verso are four lines of beautiful, very large Arabic script. It was probably sold and purchased by a Jewish scribe, who copied on both of it sides six different texts in Hebrew and Judeo-Arabic, both liturgical and documentary. 

Its content - without the Arabic text - was published in an article in the REJ in 1920 by Moise Schwab, with an introduction by Reinach. The current whereabout of the manuscripts are unknown. A photocopy of the manuscript is held at the Institutre of Hebrew Manuscripts a the National Library of Israel, and is accessible online only from within the library's building.
It seems likely that this document came for the Dār Simḥa Qaraite synagogue in Cairo, like other Arabic script court documents.

The name of the first donor was removed. Solomon's father Tovia was an official of both the Palestinian yeshiva and the Palestinian Synagogue and was mentioned in a document of 1057.
